transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Alex Mercer (CTO - Rivergate), Mia Torres (Lead ML Eng), Sam Patel (Product), Jules Park (Infra)

Auto-Summary: quick mapping of models, context length, tool-calling & deployment mode preferences; action items to run perf benchmarks and exchange security docs.

Topics: model comparison (open models), context window requirements, multilingual, tool calling (function call + RAG), hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/HSM), cost tradeoffs, next steps.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros then we'll jump into the model and deployment questions. We're about an hour but aim 45.
[00:14] Alex: Thanks Jordan. Alex here, CTO at Rivergate. We're looking at adding LLM features into our customer support and internal insights pipelines. Main questions: which open models give us the right balance of latency/cost and support our long-context docs.
[00:28] Mia: Hi all, Mia, I'm the ML lead. We heavily use embeddings + RAG today, but need a model that can do tool calls to our ticketing system and run multilingual summarization. Also we have some PII so some workloads must go private.
[00:41] Priya: Great, that's super helpful context. Quick note — Redwood supports three deployment modes: Hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools/SLA, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated data. We'll walk through model tradeoffs for each.
[00:56] Sam: timeline-wise we want a POC in next 6 weeks and possibly a pilot if numbers look good.
[01:10] Jordan: Noted. Priya do you want to take model side and Evan can cover the infra bits?
[01:18] Priya: Sure. On open models people ask about Llama 3, Mistral, RedPajama/RedPajama-Instruct and some of the new mixture models. For context length options: many models come in 8k, 32k, 64k variants. Practically the 8k are cheapest; 32k hits a sweet spot for docs; 64k is useful but more costly and less common for quantized variants.
[01:40] Mia: Our average doc chunk is 10–15k tokens when we include metadata and conversation. So 8k is often too small — we need at least 32k for the main workflows.
[01:51] Alex: Also multilingual — Spanish, Portuguese, French, and occasionally Japanese. How do those models compare?
[01:59] Priya: Llama-family (Llama 3) and Mistral have decent multilingual coverage; Mistral often performs well zero-shot in European languages. RedPajama can be okay but sometimes needs fine-tuning for Japanese. Also note inference optimizations: quantized weights affect quality differently across languages.
[02:16] Sam: On tool-calling, we need function calls into our ticketing system and a SQL extractor for product metrics. Any limitations?
[02:24] Priya: We support tool-calling via structured function calling and can integrate retrieval pipelines. For high QPS low-latency tool-calls you might want Dedicated so you can reserve capacity and avoid cold starts. Hosted can still do it but you share runtime.
[02:39] Jules: From infra side Private deployment is interesting because of compliance; we need to know KMS/HSM options and whether Redwood can integrate with our existing vault.
[02:49] Evan: Yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSMs via PKCS). We also provide audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC. We'll share the security pack.
[03:03] Alex: Great. Can you run benchmarks with our prompts?
[03:07] Priya: Absolutely. If you share 3 canonical prompt flows plus a sample doc set, we'll run Llama-3-8k, Llama-3-32k (if available), and Mistral-32k to compare latency, token cost, and quality on your prompts.
[03:21] Mia: Quality metrics — we care about hallucination rate and factuality on RAG. Do you do automated evals?
[03:28] Priya: We can run evals against your ground truth snippets and include regression checks. We'll also output token-level cost estimates and latency p50/p90.
[03:38] Jordan: Quick pause — competition question. Who are you evaluating?
[03:42] Alex: We're talking to Anthropic and doing a spot check with OpenAI for a hosted baseline; also trialing Cohere embeddings.
[03:50] Jordan: Good to know. We'll benchmark to compare apples-to-apples.
[03:55] 
[04:00] Jake (Speaker 1 - minor transcript glitch): so for the 32k case do you run prefix caching?
[04:05] Priya: Yes, Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching; if you have repeated context or long-lived sessions we can cache KV to reduce per-token compute. That helps latency for multi-turns.
[04:16] Mia: Does caching work across Dedicated pools? We have a mix of jobs.
[04:20] Evan: Dedicated pools can reserve local GPU caches; we can pin sessions and optimize kernel selection. There's also smart routing so we can route by latency or cost policy.
[04:31] Alex: What's the unit economics delta between Hosted and Dedicated for a 100k tokens/month workload?
[04:36] Jordan: We'll send a pricing sheet but rough: Hosted is pay-as-you-go with slightly higher per-token unit; Dedicated gives lower unit cost at committed throughput plus predictable latency. Private includes a platform fee and infra ops.
[04:49] Sam: For the POC we'd likely use Hosted to move fast, then Dedicated for production with Private for specific PII flows.
[04:57] Priya: That flow is common. For POC we can spin a Hosted project, run benchmarks, then propose a Dedicated reservation based on observed QPS and latency.
[05:08] 
[05:10] Alex: Any gotchas on quantization or performance with long-context models?
[05:15] Priya: Quantization helps cost but can affect quality; some models have optimized kernels for 4-bit or 8-bit. For long context you want a model with KV cache friendly execution and we test both FP16 and quantized paths. Also kernel selection differs by GPU type — A100 vs H100 — we account for that in the benchmark.
[05:34] Mia: We're on AWS with p4/p5 instances. Can Redwood Dedicated run on our cloud account?
[05:40] Evan: Dedicated is a Redwood-managed pool but we have Private options where we can deploy into your VPC or on-prem. Dedicated can also be provisioned in a customer region with isolated tenancy if required. We'll map options.
[05:52] Sam: Regarding multilingual fine-tuning, do you offer tuning or just hosting?
[05:56] Priya: We do assistance: model onboarding and light fine-tuning/adapter workflows to improve quality for languages like Japanese. For larger train jobs we'll recommend using customer's fine-tune infra and we can host the resulting artifact.
[06:08] 
[06:10] Alex: Tool-calling latency is a concern. If a function call requires a DB query, how do you avoid blocking?
[06:16] Priya: The runtime supports async tool-calls with streaming responses and partial outputs; you can also do pipelined retrieval so the LM returns a function signature and you do the call outside, then send the function result back for finalization. For strict SLAs, Dedicated reduces variability.
[06:34] Jules: For Private deployment, what's the rollout time? We can't be down for weeks.
[06:39] Evan: Private on VPC typically takes 4–6 weeks depending on approvals and network access; on-prem longer. We provide runbooks and an ops playbook for handover.
[06:50] 
[06:52] Mia: On eval metrics could you include multilingual BLEU/ROUGE-like scores?
[06:57] Priya: Yep — we can run language-specific metrics and human spot checks for high-risk languages. We'll include hallucination counts and F1 for extraction tasks.
[07:08] 
[07:10] Alex: Any red flags around data residency? We need EU-resident inference for EU customers.
[07:16] Jordan: We have region controls; Hosted can be constrained to EU region, Dedicated can be provisioned in the region and Private obviously stays in your VPC/region. We'll include region options in the security pack.
[07:29] Sam: For the benchmark, what exactly will you measure?
[07:32] Priya: We'll measure p50/p90 latency, tokens/sec throughput, per-token cost estimate, quality scores against your ground truth, memory/peak GPU footprint, and failure/error rates. We'll also test tool-call latency and concurrency.
[07:47] Mia: Can you simulate our QPS pattern? We have spiky traffic between 9–11 PST.
[07:52] Priya: Yes we'll simulate realistic load patterns and validate autoscaling and burst behavior.
[07:58] 
[08:00] Alex: A little worried about vendor lock-in — if we train adapters or fine-tune, can we export weights?
[08:05] Priya: For open models yes you can export artifacts; we support model artifacts export and versioning. For proprietary models there are T&Cs. We'll make that clear in the contract.
[08:16] 
[08:18] Jordan: Quick practical: please drop the 3 prompt examples and sample docs into the secure upload link we'll send. Also indicate which workflows must be Private.
[08:27] Mia: We'll do that. Jules will check the HSM requirement and reply.
[08:32] 
[08:34] Evan: On the runtime side one thing customers like is our smart routing + fallback: if a model variant is out of capacity we'll fall back to compatible variant automatically. For example if 32k Llama isn't available we can route to 8k with cached prefixes or to a Mistral-32k equivalent with a small quality delta.
[08:52] Sam: That fallback is nice to avoid outages.
[08:55] 
[09:00] Alex: Any suggested model picks for our mix (RAG + function calls + multilingual + 32k needs)?
[09:06] Priya: My recommendation: run Mistral-32k as primary for its multilingual and latency sweet spot, Llama-3-32k as a secondary for safety, and keep a quantized 8k variant for very cost-sensitive endpoints. If Japanese accuracy is critical consider fine-tuning RedPajama or adapter layers.
[09:25] Mia: That feels reasonable. We'll want to see the head-to-head.
[09:29] 
[09:30] Jordan: Let's capture next steps: Redwood runs the benchmark, send security docs and pricing, Rivergate shares prompts + docs, schedule follow-up deep dive.
[09:41] Alex: Agreed. Anything else?
[09:44] Mia: One small question — embeddings: are you recommending Redwood embeddings or external? We currently use Cohere but could consolidate.
[09:52] Priya: We support multiple embeddings and have our own optimized embeddings; cost/quality tradeoffs depend. We'll include a quick AB test in the benchmark.
[10:02] 
[10:05] Jordan: Cool, we'll follow up with an email that includes the upload link and timelines. Thanks everyone.
[10:11] Alex: Thanks all.
[10:13] [END]

Notes and minor transcript errors: occasional misrecognized words (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache; "Red Pajama" sometimes transcribed as "Red Pajama" correctly but other brand names slightly off). There are overlaps where Speaker 1 appears due to recording artifact.
